transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve felt low and weighed down almost all the time for the last couple of years, and it just never really lifts. My primary care doctor suggested I come speak with you because it's starting to affect my life.
During these past two years, have you had any periods lasting more than two months where your mood returned to normal and you felt like your usual self?

No, I haven't had any periods of relief that lasted anywhere near that long. This heavy feeling has been pretty much continuous since a few weeks after our move two years ago, and any lighter moments have only lasted for a few days at most.
Before these past two years, have you ever experienced other periods in your life where you felt deeply depressed for weeks or months at a time?
No, I haven't really experienced anything like this before our move two years ago. This level of persistent low mood is completely new to me, and I've never felt this way in the past.
Along with this low mood over the past two years, have you noticed other changes like low energy, sleep problems, poor appetite, or feelings of low self-esteem?

Yes, the lack of energy is overwhelming—even when I sleep a full eight hours, I feel like I’m wading through molasses and simple tasks completely wipe me out. I haven't really noticed major changes in my appetite or self-esteem specifically. It's just this constant, heavy fatigue that leaves me feeling drained every single day.
Have you also noticed any difficulties with concentrating or making decisions, or have you been feeling hopeless about the future during these past two years?

Yes, my brain feels like it’s in a constant fog; I struggle to absorb what I'm reading at work, lose my train of thought in meetings, and even second-guess simple decisions like what to wear or make for dinner. I also feel really hopeless about the future, like I'm just stuck in this numb place, so I've stopped making plans because it feels like nothing I do will change how flat everything is.
During these past two years, have you struggled with feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, or have you had any thoughts of death or self-harm?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of self-harm or death. And while I feel very down and stuck, I wouldn't say I've experienced intense feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt.
Have you experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in almost all of the activities, hobbies, or social interactions that you used to enjoy?

Yes, I've lost interest in almost everything. Things I used to love, like precision baking, stargazing with my telescope, and detailed travel planning, now just feel like chores or obligations. I’ve even stopped going to our neighborhood plant-swap gatherings because I just don't have the energy to socialize anymore.

You mentioned sleeping eight hours, but have you experienced any actual changes in your sleep patterns, such as difficulty falling asleep, waking up in the middle of the night, or sleeping much more than usual?

I haven't really noticed major changes like difficulty falling asleep or waking up in the night, and I still get a full eight hours of sleep. However, despite getting a full night's sleep, I still wake up feeling completely exhausted and wiped out, as if I'm wading through molasses.
Have you or those close to you noticed that you are speaking or moving much more slowly than usual, or conversely, that you seem unusually restless and unable to sit still?
No, I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking slowly, nor have I felt unusually restless or unable to sit still. No one in my life has mentioned anything like that to me either.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight, such as losing or gaining weight without trying, during these past two years?
No, I haven't noticed any significant changes in my weight over the last two years. My appetite has stayed pretty much the same, so that hasn't really been an issue for me.
When these feelings first started after your move two years ago, did they set in suddenly and feel very intense right away, or did they develop gradually as a milder, constant heaviness?

It definitely developed gradually rather than setting in all at once. It started a few weeks after our move and slowly grew into this constant, heavy, weighed-down feeling that hasn't let up over the last two years.
Have you noticed if your low mood is typically worse in the morning, or have you experienced a significant decrease in your sex drive since these feelings began?

I'm not really sure or haven't thought about whether my mood is worse in the morning specifically, since it just feels heavy and gray from the moment I wake up. I also haven't really paid attention to or noticed any specific changes in my sex drive.
During these past two years, did you ever experience a period of two weeks or more where your depression became much more severe, making it extremely difficult to function at all?

No, I haven't experienced a specific two-week period where the depression suddenly spiked or became much more severe. It has just been a very steady, continuous heaviness that has stayed at this same low baseline the entire time.
Have you ever experienced a period of several days or more where you felt the opposite of depressed—such as having unusually high energy, feeling on top of the world, or needing very little sleep?

No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never had periods of unusually high energy, feeling on top of the world, or needing very little sleep. My state has just been consistently low and heavy.
Do you have any medical conditions, like thyroid problems, or do you take any medications or substances regularly that could be affecting your energy and mood?
No, I don't have any known medical conditions like thyroid issues. I also don't take any regular medications or substances that could be causing these symptoms.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a continuous, low-grade depressed mood lasting for two years, with no symptom-free periods exceeding two months. The onset was gradual, occurring shortly after a psychosocial stressor (moving). The presentation is characterized by overwhelming fatigue, concentration difficulties, hopelessness, and a significant loss of interest in activities and social interactions. The symptoms have remained at a steady baseline without meeting the criteria for a severe depressive episode, and there is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, nor any medical or substance-related causes. This clinical picture is diagnostic of Dysthymia (F34.1).
